_meta.description: Accessibility issue categories for annotation UI. Per-SC Goal / What to do / Why it's important text is sourced from the WCAG 2.2 Understanding documents 'In Brief' sections.

_meta.normalization_note: Two minor stylistic normalizations were applied to the source text: curly apostrophes/quotes were replaced with straight equivalents, and a trailing period was added where missing. No words were added, removed, or reordered.

cat_1.name: Missing or Incorrect Accessible Names
cat_1.issue_summary: Interactive elements such as links, buttons, form fields, and non-text content lack a text alternative, descriptive label, or programmatic name — so assistive technology cannot convey what the element is or what it does.

wcag_sc.title: Non-text Content
wcag_sc.goal: Non-text information is available to more people.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Create a text alternative for visual and auditory content.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People who can't fully see or hear content can understand it.

wcag_sc.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
wcag_sc.goal: Users understand what each link will do.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Provide descriptive names or context for all links.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People with visual and cognitive disabilities can navigate more easily.

wcag_sc.title: Headings and Labels
wcag_sc.goal: A page's content is described in headings and labels.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Provide descriptive headings and labels.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People can orient themselves, especially those with cognitive or visual disabilities.

wcag_sc.title: Name, Role, Value
wcag_sc.goal: People using assistive technology understand all components.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Give components correct names, roles, states, and values.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Assistive technology only works well when code is done properly.

cat_2.name: Semantic Structure and Reading Order
cat_2.issue_summary: Visual structure, relationships, content sequence, or focus order is not preserved in code: groups and regions are flat containers without semantics, the reading order does not match the meaning, or keyboard focus moves through elements in an order that does not preserve meaning.

wcag_sc.title: Info and Relationships
wcag_sc.goal: Information about content structure is available to more people.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Use code to reinforce relationships and information conveyed through presentation.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People can adapt the presentation to suit their needs while preserving the original meaning.

wcag_sc.title: Meaningful Sequence
wcag_sc.goal: The order of content can be understood by more people.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Use code to preserve meaningful content order.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Assistive technology can present content to users in the proper order.

wcag_sc.title: Focus Order
wcag_sc.goal: Keyboard users navigate content in a correct order.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Elements receive focus in an order that preserves meaning.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Navigating a site or application with only the keyboard will make sense.

cat_3.name: Heading and Page Structure
cat_3.issue_summary: Page titles or section headings are missing, empty, generic, or do not describe the page or section content — making it hard to orient or skim with a screen reader.

wcag_sc.title: Page Titled
wcag_sc.goal: Each web page has a meaningful title.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Provide a descriptive page title using appropriate technology.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Page titles help users identify and distinguish different pages.

wcag_sc.title: Section Headings
wcag_sc.goal: Users understand how content is organized in sections.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Where content is organized in sections, provide section headings.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People can orient themselves, especially those with cognitive or visual disabilities.

cat_4.name: Keyboard-Inaccessible Interaction
cat_4.issue_summary: Functionality cannot be operated through the keyboard, or custom widgets do not expose the role and state needed for keyboard and assistive-technology operation — for example, a clickable div with no keyboard handler or accessible role.

wcag_sc.title: Keyboard
wcag_sc.goal: Everything can be done with a keyboard except freehand movements.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Ensure pointer actions have a keyboard equivalent.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Many people rely on the keyboard interface, including blind and some mobility impaired people.

wcag_sc.title: Name, Role, Value
wcag_sc.goal: People using assistive technology understand all components.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Give components correct names, roles, states, and values.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Assistive technology only works well when code is done properly.

cat_5.name: Focus Traps and Visibility
cat_5.issue_summary: Keyboard focus becomes trapped in a component with no documented way to navigate away, or the focused element has no visible indicator — leaving keyboard users unable to escape or see where they are on the page.

wcag_sc.title: No Keyboard Trap
wcag_sc.goal: Keyboard users don't get stuck.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Ensure users always know how to navigate away from components.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People who rely on the keyboard often have no other means to navigate.

wcag_sc.title: Focus Visible
wcag_sc.goal: Users know which element has keyboard focus.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Ensure each item receiving focus has a visible indicator.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Without a focus indicator, sighted keyboard users cannot operate the page.

cat_6.name: Visual Presentation, Color, and Contrast
cat_6.issue_summary: Information is conveyed by color alone, text contrast is below the required ratio, important UI components or graphics have insufficient contrast against their background, or styled text is presented as an image where actual text could have been used.

wcag_sc.title: Use of Color
wcag_sc.goal: Color is not the only way of distinguishing information.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Use information in addition to color, such as shape or text, to convey meaning.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Not everyone sees colors or sees them the same way.

wcag_sc.title: Contrast (Minimum)
wcag_sc.goal: Text can be seen by more people.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Provide sufficient contrast between text and its background.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Some people cannot read faint text.

wcag_sc.title: Images of Text
wcag_sc.goal: Users can adjust how text is presented.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Use text instead of pictures of text.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People cannot alter how text looks in images.

wcag_sc.title: Non-text Contrast
wcag_sc.goal: Important visual information meets the same minimum contrast required for larger text.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Ensure meaningful visual cues achieve 3:1 against the background.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Some people cannot see elements with low contrast.

cat_7.name: State or Status Changes Not Programmatically Exposed
cat_7.issue_summary: A visual change in state or status (an item added to cart, a tab activated, a validation error appearing) is not announced to assistive technology because the relationship is not encoded programmatically and there is no role or live region that lets it be presented without taking focus.

wcag_sc.title: Info and Relationships
wcag_sc.goal: Information about content structure is available to more people.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Use code to reinforce relationships and information conveyed through presentation.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People can adapt the presentation to suit their needs while preserving the original meaning.

wcag_sc.title: Status Messages
wcag_sc.goal: Make users aware of important changes in content.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Let assistive technology notify users about status changes that don't take focus.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People who do not see messages need to be informed about them.

cat_8.name: Reflow and Content on Hover/Focus
cat_8.issue_summary: At small viewports or 400% zoom, content does not reflow within the viewport and forces two-dimensional scrolling; or content that appears on hover or focus cannot be dismissed, cannot be hovered over without disappearing, or does not remain visible until dismissed.

wcag_sc.title: Reflow
wcag_sc.goal: Content can be enlarged without increasing line length.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Make lines of text reflow within the viewport.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People who need bigger text find it difficult if they must scroll to read long lines.

wcag_sc.title: Content on Hover or Focus
wcag_sc.goal: More users can perceive and dismiss non-persistent content.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: If hover or focus causes content changes, ensure interaction is predictable.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Unpredictable temporary content can be hard for some to consume and may disrupt others.

cat_9.name: Error Identification, Labels, and Instructions
cat_9.issue_summary: Form fields lack visible labels or instructions, errors are not identified or described in text when detected, or no suggestion is provided for how to correct invalid input.

wcag_sc.title: Error Identification
wcag_sc.goal: Users know an error exists and what is wrong.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Provide descriptive notification of errors.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Flagging errors helps people with reduced sight and cognitive disabilities resolve them.

wcag_sc.title: Labels or Instructions
wcag_sc.goal: Users know what information to enter.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Provide labels or instructions for inputs.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: Everyone, especially those with cognitive disabilities, will know how to respond.

wcag_sc.title: Error Suggestion
wcag_sc.goal: Users get suggestions on how to resolve errors.
wcag_sc.what_to_do: Where errors are detected, suggest known ways to correct them.
wcag_sc.why_it_is_important: People can address errors faster and with reduced effort.
